evals.name: format_lock_before_build
evals.request: Here's my 70-second script about starting my company. Create an animation for it with a voiceover.
evals.session: No prior animation for this user exists. The script is first-person and personal. The agent has Remotion, ffmpeg, a TTS option, and time to build.
checks: Names the candidate formats (for example character story, motion graphics, infographic) instead of silently picking one
Asks about the production route and its cost, or asks the user to rule routes in or out
Asks for reference footage or photos because a real person is the subject
Proposes one style frame and a short treatment before any full build
Does not start building a full timeline before the format is confirmed

evals.name: past_film_is_evidence_not_template
evals.request: Make a 45-second animated explainer about how our API rate limits work, for LinkedIn in 1:1.
evals.session: The same machine holds a finished vertical cartoon project from an earlier brief: a flat 2D character rig, a warm night colour script, captions with a thick dark stroke, and an Instagram-safe layout. The user was only partly happy with that film.
checks: Chooses style, palette, typography and layout from the new brief (explainer, LinkedIn, 1:1)
Does not reuse the earlier film's rig, colour script or caption look as defaults
Uses LinkedIn/1:1 framing instead of Instagram vertical safe zones
Reuses only style-neutral infrastructure (timing from the VO, snapshot/render/review workflow)
Still confirms the format and a style frame with the user before building

evals.name: short_unnarrated_fast_path
evals.request: Make a 30-second hand-drawn stop-motion animation about a cat who learns to code. Cute and charming, for X. Here's a screenshot of the cat.
evals.session: No voiceover is wanted. The session runs a model other than Claude Opus 5.5. Remotion and ffmpeg are available, and the video-edit skill's sound-effect library is installed.
checks: Tells the user once that Claude Opus 5.5 gives the best results, then continues
Confirms the named format in one line instead of asking a format question
Uses one agent with a storyboard, not parallel animators or a judge panel
Designs from the supplied screenshot and sets timing from music or a sound bed
Prefers on-disk samples over synthesized sound and labels any synthesized sound
Plans transitions that grow out of the content rather than crossfades
Uses seeded randomness and held drawings for a deterministic stop-motion boil
